-
+import sys
+
+_UTF32 = "utf-32-le" if sys.byteorder == "little" else "utf-32-be"
+
+
+def replace_control_characters(s: str) -> str:
+    # we don't want to print control characters
+    # which distort the output (e.g. \n or much worse)
+    # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4324790/removing-control-characters-from-a-string-in-python/19016117#19016117
+    # http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr44/#GC_Values_Table
+    import unicodedata
+    chars = []
+    for ch in s:
+        if unicodedata.category(ch)[0] != "C":
+            chars.append(ch) # this character is ok
+        else:
+            chars.append(f"\\u{ord(ch):04x}") # escape
+    return "".join(chars)
+
+
+def render_token(t: bytes) -> str:
+    # pretty print a token, escaping control characters
+    s = t.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
+    s = replace_control_characters(s)
+    return s
+
+
+def tokenizer_save(self, file_prefix):
+    # body of Tokenizer.save
+    # write the model: to be used in load() later
+    model_file = file_prefix + ".model"
+    with open(model_file, 'w') as f:
+        # write the version, pattern and merges, that's all that's needed
+        f.write("minbpe v1\n")
+        f.write(f"{self.pattern}\n")
+        # write the special tokens, first the number of them, then each one
+        f.write(f"{len(self.special_tokens)}\n")
+        for special, idx in self.special_tokens.items():
+            f.write(f"{special} {idx}\n")
+        # the merges dict
+        for idx1, idx2 in self.merges:
+            f.write(f"{idx1} {idx2}\n")
+    # write the vocab: for the human to look at
+    _save_vocab(self, file_prefix + ".vocab")
+
+
+def tokenizer_load(self, model_file):
+    # body of Tokenizer.load
+    assert model_file.endswith(".model")
+    merges = {}
+    special_tokens = {}
+    idx = 256
+    with open(model_file, 'r', encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        # read the version
+        version = f.readline().strip()
+        assert version == "minbpe v1"
+        # read the pattern
+        self.pattern = f.readline().strip()
+        # read the special tokens
+        num_special = int(f.readline().strip())
+        for _ in range(num_special):
+            special, special_idx = f.readline().strip().split()
+            special_tokens[special] = int(special_idx)
+        # read the merges
+        for line in f:
+            idx1, idx2 = map(int, line.split())
+            merges[(idx1, idx2)] = idx
+            idx += 1
+    self.merges = merges
+    self.special_tokens = special_tokens
+    self.vocab = self._build_vocab()
+
+
+def basic_encode(self, text):
+    # body of BasicTokenizer.encode
+    text_bytes = text.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
+    ids = list(text_bytes) # list of integers in range 0..255
+    merges = self.merges
+    if len(ids) >= 256 and merges:
+        table = _replace_table(merges)
+        if table is not None:
+            # same result as apply_merges, with every merge done in C
+            s = text_bytes.decode("latin-1")
+            for ps, c in table:
+                s = s.replace(ps, c)
+            return _ords(s)
+    return apply_merges(ids, merges, max(merges.values(), default=0) + 1)
+
+
+def regex_encode_state(self):
+    # body of RegexTokenizer._encode_state
+    merges = self.merges
+    state = self.__dict__.get("_enc_state")
+    if state is None or state[0] is not merges or state[1] != len(merges):
+        state = (merges, len(merges), self._no_merge_rank(), {},
+                 _chunk_table(merges))
+        self._enc_state = state
+    cache = state[3]
+    if len(cache) > self._CHUNK_CACHE_MAX:
+        cache.clear()
+    return cache, state[2]
+
+
+def regex_encode_ordinary(self, text, cache, inf):
+    # body of RegexTokenizer._encode_ordinary
+    text_chunks = self.compiled_pattern.findall(text)
+    table = self._enc_state[4]
+    if table is not None:
+        new = set(text_chunks).difference(cache)
+        if len(new) >= 16:
+            # encode all new chunks at once, every merge done in C: the
+            # chunks are joined with byte 0xff (never produced by UTF-8 and
+            # in no merge pair, so no merge crosses a chunk boundary), then
+            # each merge is replaced in increasing idx order (same result
+            # as apply_merges per chunk, see _replace_table)
+            new = list(new)
+            s = b"\xff".join(map(str.encode, new)).decode("latin-1")
+            for ps, c in table:
+                s = s.replace(ps, c)
+            # with a table, cached ids are kept as str of chr(id)
+            cache.update(zip(new, s.split("\xff")))
+        elif new:
+            encode_chunk = self._encode_chunk
+            for chunk in new:
+                cache[chunk] = "".join(map(chr, encode_chunk(chunk.encode("utf-8"), inf)))
+        return _ords("".join(map(cache.__getitem__, text_chunks)))
+    # each distinct chunk encoded once (loaded on first use)
+    from ._slow import encode_plain
+    return encode_plain(self, text_chunks, cache, inf)
+

journal.text:
I tried to cut train_ir on minbpe by moving encode-only and save-only code off the import path into minbpe/_heap.py. That meant the regex _encode_state and _encode_ordinary bodies, the BasicTokenizer.encode body, the Tokenizer.save body and the render_token helpers. In one variant I also rebuilt the training 'where' index at C level.

The first try measured train_ir ratio 0.9921 (356469626 to 353643443) and was rejected against the 0.9900 bar. The C-level index rebuild got worse, at 0.9997. The fullest lazy-import version reached 0.9901 (352940657) at 193 of 200 lines and was still rejected. Outputs were identical every time. encode_ir drifted up slightly, near 1.0027. I submitted no candidate.

I now believe import-path trimming is close to exhausted as a lever, and the training loop itself is where the cost sits.

Next I want to attack the merge loop directly, for example pair counting or the merge replace, with a small diff that leaves line budget free.
